stem: Which of the following is a statistical question?
options: How many legs does a spider have?
How many hours do Grade 7 students in our school sleep at night?
What is the exact height of the main door of our classroom today?
On which day of the week does our school hold its weekly assembly?
explanation: Correct option: (B). Different students sleep for different numbers of hours, so the answer needs data to be collected and analysed; that makes it a statistical question. A spider always has eight legs, the door has one fixed height, and the assembly day is a single fact, so each of these has one answer and needs no data.

stem: A statistical statement is a claim or summary about some phenomenon that is expressed in terms of
options: numerical values, proportions, probabilities or predictions
personal likes and dislikes, without using any numbers
rules that hold true in every single case without exception
definitions of words that are used in mathematics
explanation: Correct option: (A). The chapter describes a statistical statement as a claim or summary about some phenomenon expressed through numerical values, proportions, probabilities or predictions, for example 'David spends about 7 hours daily in school'. Likes and dislikes without numbers, rules true in every case, and definitions are not summaries of data.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a statistical question?
options: How old are the dogs that live on this street?
What fraction of the students in your class like walking up a hill?
Do you like reading?

The ages of different dogs, the fraction of students in a class, and the rainfall over many days of a year all vary and must be answered by collecting data, so they are statistical questions.

stem: Which of the following is a statistical statement?
options: A square always has four sides that are all of equal length.
Seven is an odd number and eight is an even number.
The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home.
explanation: Correct option: (D). Cycling time changes from day to day, and 'about 15 minutes' is a numerical summary of that experience, so it is a statistical statement. The facts about a square and about odd and even numbers are always true by definition, and the direction of sunrise is a fixed fact; none of them summarises varying data.

Collect onion prices in both towns over many months and analyse them.

explanation: Correct option: (D). Total = 7 + 2 + 5 + 6 = 20 mangoes. Fair share = 20 / 4 = 5 mangoes each, which is the mean. 7 is the largest collection, 6 is one friend's count, and 4 is the number of friends, so none of them is the equal share.

stem: Nikhil's times (in seconds) for a 100 m race over a week were 17, 18, 17, 16, 19, 17, 18. Sunil's times were 20, 18, 18, 17, 16, 16, 17. Who ran quicker on average?
options: Neither; their average times are the same.
Nikhil, because his slowest time is only 19 s.
Sunil, because his best time is 16 s twice.
Nikhil, because he ran 17 s most often.
explanation: Correct option: (A). Nikhil: 17 + 18 + 17 + 16 + 19 + 17 + 18 = 122, so mean = 122 / 7 = about 17.43 s. Sunil: 20 + 18 + 18 + 17 + 16 + 16 + 17 = 122, so mean = 122 / 7 = about 17.43 s. The averages are equal. The slowest time, the best time and the most frequent time each look at only part of the data.

stem: A player's scores in a series are 57, 13, 0, 84, -, 51, 27, where '-' means the player did not play Match 5. What is the player's average score per match?
options: 232 / 7, which is about 33.14 runs
232 / 6, which is about 38.67 runs
232 / 5, which is exactly 46.40 runs
175 / 6, which is about 29.17 runs
explanation: Correct option: (B). Total = 57 + 13 + 0 + 84 + 51 + 27 = 232. The 0 in Match 3 is a real score, so that match counts, but Match 5 was not played, so it does not. Number of matches = 6, and mean = 232 / 6 = about 38.67 runs. Dividing by 7 counts the missed match, dividing by 5 drops the zero score, and 175 is a wrong total.

stem: The mean of five numbers is 24. Four of the numbers are 20, 25, 30 and 18. What is the fifth number?
explanation: Correct option: (A). If the mean of five numbers is 24, their total is 5 x 24 = 120. The four known numbers add up to 20 + 25 + 30 + 18 = 93, so the fifth number is 120 - 93 = 27. 24 just repeats the mean, 23 is 93 / 4 rounded (the mean of the four known numbers), and 30 is the largest given value.

stem: In a collection of data, an outlier is a value that
options: lies exactly in the middle of the sorted values
differs greatly from most of the other values
occurs more often than any of the other values
is equal to the mean of all the other values

Mean about 18.29 and median 22

stem: For Poovizhi's family (170, 173, 165, 118, 175 cm), the mean is 160.2 cm and the median is 170 cm. If the outlier 118 cm is removed, how do the mean and the median change?
options: The mean rises by about 10.5 cm; the median rises by only 1.5 cm.
The mean rises by only 1.5 cm; the median rises by about 10.5 cm.
The mean and the median both rise by about 10.5 cm each.
The mean rises by about 10.5 cm; the median stays at 170 cm.
explanation: Correct option: (A). Without 118: mean = (170 + 173 + 165 + 175) / 4 = 683 / 4 = 170.75 cm, a rise of about 10.5 cm. Sorted: 165, 170, 173, 175, so median = (170 + 173) / 2 = 171.5 cm, a rise of only 1.5 cm. An outlier pulls the mean strongly but hardly moves the median; the other options reverse this, make both change equally, or forget that the median of four values is the average of the middle two.

stem: The mean and the median are called measures of central tendency because they
options: show only the largest and smallest values of the data
represent the centre around which the values pile up
give the total of all the values in the data collected
show the original order in which the data was collected
explanation: Correct option: (B). Central tendency is the tendency of the values to pile up around a particular value; the mean and median represent this 'centre' of the data. The largest and smallest values are extremes, the total is a sum, and the original order is lost in summaries such as these.

stem: In a Grade 5 class, the boys' heights lie between 128 cm and 158 cm, and the girls' heights lie between 136 cm and 156 cm. By how much do the tallest and shortest boys differ in height?
options: 20 cm
22 cm
30 cm
8 cm

Difference for boys = 158 - 128 = 30 cm. 20 cm is the girls' difference (156 - 136), 22 cm is the tallest boy minus the shortest girl (158 - 136), and 8 cm is the shortest girl minus the shortest boy (136 - 128). stem: In a cricket innings, the median runs scored by the 11 batters of a team was 0, yet the team scored 407 runs. What must be true?
options: Exactly 1 of the 11 batters scored 0 runs.
The average score of the batters was 0 runs.
No batter scored more than 37 runs in the innings.
At least 6 of the 11 batters scored 0 runs.
explanation: Correct option: (D). With 11 sorted scores, the median is the 6th value. For it to be 0, the 6th score and all the scores below it must be 0, so at least 6 batters scored 0; the remaining few batters made almost all of the 407 runs. One zero would not make the median 0, the mean is far above 0 because the total is 407, and some batters must have scored much more than 37.

stem: Two groups of children estimated the length of 1 minute. Group A had mean 58.21 s and median 60 s; Group B had mean 59.28 s and median 59.5 s. Which statement is best supported by these values?
options: In Group A, a few low estimates pulled the mean below the median.
In Group A, a few high estimates pulled the mean above the median.
Every child in Group B estimated the minute better than Group A.
Half the children in Group B opened their eyes after 59.28 s.
explanation: Correct option: (A). In Group A the mean (58.21) is clearly below the median (60), which happens when some values at the lower end pull the mean down. High values would push the mean above the median, summary values cannot tell us about every child, and it is the median (59.5), not the mean, that splits Group B into two halves.

stem: A tap's daily water use (in litres) was 5.6, 8, 3.09, 12.9, 6.5, 12.1, 11.3, 20.5 and 7.4. Can the mean or the median of this data lie between 25 and 30?
options: Yes, because the maximum value 20.5 is quite close to the lower limit 25.
No, because both must lie between the minimum 3.09 and the maximum 20.5.
Yes, the mean can lie there, but the median can never lie there.
No, because the mean must always be equal to the median here.
explanation: Correct option: (B). The mean balances the highs and lows and the median is a middle value, so neither can be smaller than the minimum (3.09) or larger than the maximum (20.5); a value between 25 and 30 is impossible. Being 'close' to 25 does not matter, the mean is also bounded by the extremes, and the mean and median need not be equal.

stem: City 1 gets about 18 hours of daylight per day in June and about 6 hours in December. City 2 gets about 9 hours per day in June and about 15 hours in December. What is the best explanation of this pattern?
options: Both cities lie on the Equator, but one is at a higher altitude.
Both cities are in the Northern Hemisphere, at different longitudes.
City 2 lies close to the Equator and City 1 lies close to a pole.
The cities are in opposite hemispheres, both far from the Equator.
explanation: Correct option: (D). City 1 has its longest days in June and City 2 has its shortest days in June, so their seasons are inverted; this happens when the cities are in opposite hemispheres (City 1 is Helsinki in the north, City 2 is Wellington in the south). The large variation shows both are far from the Equator. Places on the Equator have nearly equal days all year, two northern cities would have summer at the same time, and a city near the Equator would not vary from 9 to 15 hours.

stem: Average heights (cm) from a survey: 13-year-old girls in 1989: 143.2; 14-year-old girls in 2009: 148; 15-year-old boys in 2019: 159; 16-year-old boys in 1989: 158.9; 13-year-old girls in 2019: 147.7. Which statement can be justified using this data?

stem: A school has two Grade 7 sections, each with 15 boys and 15 girls. In one section, the mean height of the students is 154.2 cm. What must be true about the mean height of the other section?
options: It must be exactly the same, that is, 154.2 cm.
It cannot be determined from the information given.
It must be less than 154.2 cm, since girls are shorter.
It must be more than 154.2 cm, since boys are taller.
explanation: Correct option: (B). The mean depends on the actual heights of the 30 students in the other section, and no data about them is given; having the same number of boys and girls does not make the heights the same. So none of 'equal', 'less' or 'more' must be true, and the mean cannot be determined. Also, averages of boys and girls differ by age, so 'boys are taller' or 'girls are shorter' cannot be assumed.
